name: Cory Walsh
life: “I still remember the first match Dad let me choose.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the approach to Seabright Court, where Cory likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I brought a pocket radio so two roommates can listen to different matches and still keep score together.
appearance: Cory has a long face and high cheekbones. Look for a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a gray fisher's sweater with a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. In conversation Cory leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations.
personality: Cory has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To bring two pocket sets to the shared room.
family: Toby Lin is Cory’s half-sibling. Cory is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Toby calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The wrong bicycle*, Toby says, “I docked the courier for arriving late. His customer had watched the entire mix-up.”
connections: Linden Lewis. They arrange a shared score without making the entire ward hear the same game.

reactions.situation: The replacement radio drowns out a patient's match
reactions.response: Cory asks the two patients which part of the match each wants to hear.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Cory asks which apartment is expecting someone home and makes sure that household knows about the delay.

reactions.situation: When somebody trades on a title
reactions.response: Cory asks for the name of the person who will still be around tomorrow.
